series.concept: Holly unwraps and reacts to a finished customer order before it goes out, narrating why the personalisation makes it better than anything you'd find on the high street.
series.name: That'll Do Nicely

series.concept: A fortnightly "gift matchmaking" format where Holly presents a specific ROR product and the audience votes in comments on which person in their life deserves it.
series.name: Right, Who's Getting This

series.concept: A behind-the-scenes mini-documentary series following one product from customer brief to finished item — design, print or embroidery, quality check, pack and dispatch.
series.name: From Blank to Brilliant

series.concept: A fortnightly outfit/styling format where Holly builds a real, wearable outfit around one ROR piece — no fashion influencer energy, just actual clothes a 35-45 year old woman owns.
series.name: She'd Absolutely Wear That

series.concept: A weekly peek behind the curtain at the genuinely unglamorous reality of running a small print-on-demand business — one honest, unfiltered moment per week, 30 seconds max.
series.name: 30 Seconds of Chaos

series.concept: Customers or followers submit a real gifting brief in the comments — who it's for, what they're like, what the occasion is — and Holly designs a personalised concept live on camera, talking through her thinking.
series.name: The Brief

series.concept: Holly reviews a generic, mass-market gift (from Amazon, a supermarket, or a pound shop) against the equivalent personalised ROR alternative — no cruelty, just honest comparison with northern deadpan humour.
series.name: Gift or Grim

series.concept: Holly reads out a real, chaotic, relatable customer text or DM brief — "it's for my mate Karen, she's obsessed with her dog and her wine and she turns 50 in three weeks" — and talks through exactly why personalisation beats panic-buying a Boots gift set.
series.name: Text Me The Brief

series.concept: A fortnightly look at design ideas, slogans, or product concepts that got binned — too niche, too risky, too unhinged — with Bethan and Holly explaining why they didn't make the cut.
series.name: The Reject Pile

series.concept: A weekly customer story format — Holly shares the real person behind a recent order, the occasion, the relationship, the detail that made the personalisation matter — no names, just the warmth.
series.name: Who Actually Buys This

series.concept: A monthly check-in where Holly pulls up a photo, a screenshot, or a memory from the same week the previous year and talks honestly about what's changed, what hasn't, and what running ROR actually looks like over time.
series.name: This Time Last Year

series.concept: Holly presents three to five possible new slogans or personalisation options ROR is considering adding — some brilliant, some questionable — and asks the audience to vote on which ones get made into real products.
series.name: Steal This Slogan

series.concept: A fortnightly gifting ritual series where Holly shows a complete, thoughtful, personalised gift being put together from scratch — product choice, packaging, the personal touch — in real time, under ten minutes.
series.name: Wrapped In Ten Minutes

series.concept: A fortnightly series where real ROR customers — not influencers, not models — film themselves getting dressed for an actual real occasion in a ROR piece, submitted by the customer and shared with their permission.
series.name: Normal Women Getting Dressed

series.concept: A fortnightly series where Bethan pitches Holly a wild or unexpected product/slogan idea and Holly reacts, debates it, and they decide together whether it lives or dies — all on camera.
series.name: Bethan Made Me Do It

series.concept: A fortnightly series where Holly picks one specific ROR product and imagines — out loud, with deadpan northern logic — the exact type of person who buys it, the occasion, the group chat that led to the purchase.
series.name: Who Actually Buys This?

series.concept: A weekly series where one ROR product — same item, same slogan — gets shown in three completely different real-life contexts, styled and used differently, proving personalised pieces aren't precious.
series.name: Same Bag, Different Life

series.concept: A fortnightly series where Holly solves one specific gifting panic — a real scenario, a real deadline, a real type of person — and builds the case for why personalised beats purchased, step by step.
series.name: The Guilt-Free Gift Guide

series.concept: A fortnightly storytelling series where Holly reads a real message — a review, a thank-you DM, a photo caption — from a customer describing the moment the recipient opened their ROR gift, then talks honestly about why that moment is the whole point.
series.name: You Can't Buy This Feeling

series.concept: A weekly series where Holly takes a real, generic, mass-market gift slogan — from a card shop, a supermarket aisle, a Moonpig suggestion — and rewrites it live on camera into something that actually sounds like a real person gave it thought.
series.name: Slogan Surgery

series.concept: A fortnightly behind-the-scenes local series where Holly shows one small, specific, unglamorous detail of running a physical small business in Bury — the suppliers, the high street, the van, the post office queue — that most customers never think about.
series.name: Bury to Your Door

series.concept: Holly digs out a real, existing mass-market slogan product — a mug, a card, a cushion — traces where the phrase originally came from, and explains why it's now completely meaningless through overuse.
series.name: Slogan Archaeology

series.concept: Holly reconstructs the original customer brief behind a real ROR order — what the buyer asked for, what they were trying to say, and how the design team translated it into something that actually landed.
series.name: The Brief That Built It

series.concept: A fortnightly series where Holly picks one upcoming calendar moment — a birthday, a seasonal occasion, a random gifting spike — and talks honestly about what people are actually trying to say when they buy a gift for it.
series.name: What Are We Buying This For

series.concept: A fortnightly series where Bethan explains — on camera, in plain terms — one real design or colour decision that went into an ROR product, and why it matters more than customers realise.
series.name: Bethan's Unhinged Colour Theory

series.concept: Holly buys one real product from a high street or online gifting brand each fortnight and reviews it as a gift — not for laughs, but honestly — looking at personalisation potential, longevity, and whether it actually says anything about the person receiving it.
series.name: I Bought It So You Don't Have To

series.concept: A weekly series where Holly films one single moment from the current working day — not a process, not a product reveal, just one real, specific, unremarkable thing that happened — and says what it made her think about.
series.name: Thirty Seconds From The Packing Table

series.concept: A fortnightly series where Holly takes one very specific real-life occasion — not just "birthday" but "my mate's turning 40 and she's going through a divorce and we want it to feel fun not sad" — and builds the entire gifting logic out loud from scratch.
series.name: The Occasion Audit
